items.text: Ní ọjọ́ kan, Anansi aláǹtakùn mú àwọn iṣu láti ọgbà-oko rẹ̀.Àwọn iṣu aládùn kù, nítorí náà ó dín wọn dáradára lórí iná. Lẹ́hìn náà, ó jòkó láti jẹ wọ́n.

translation_en.text:
One day, Anansi the spider picked
some yams from his garden.
They were extra beautiful delicious
yams, so he baked them carefully in
the fire.
Then he sat down to eat them up.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0005_anansi-ati-ijapa.md p1; Text: Ghanaian folktale; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

claims.locator: raw/asp/yo/0005_anansi-ati-ijapa.md p1; Text: Ghanaian folktale; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

items.label: beta

items.text: Ṣùgbọ́n láí sí àwọn òkúta ní àpò rẹ̀ láti mu dúró sí ìsàlẹ̀ odò náà, omi gbé Anansi lọ sí ojú omi padà. Anansi fi ojú rẹ̀ sínú omi, o sì rí bí Ìjàpá ṣe jẹ gbogbo aládùn náà.

translation_en.text:
But without the rocks in his pockets
to hold him down, Anansi floated
right back to the surface of the river
again, and popped out of the water.
Anansi sadly put his head down into
the water and watched Turtle eat up
all of the delicious food!

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0005_anansi-ati-ijapa.md p10; Text: Ghanaian folktale; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

items.text: Ní ìgbà kan, Ìjàpá àti Ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ jẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́ tímọ́tímọ́. Ní ọjọ́ kan lẹ́yìn oúnjẹ, Ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ bi Ìjàpá, “Ọ̀rẹ́ mi, ọjọ́ ọjà ti fẹ́ dé ṣùgbọ́n a kò ní owó. Irú iṣẹ́ wo ni a lè ṣe láti pa owó?”

translation_en.text:
Once upon a time,

Tortoise and Squirrel were very close friends.

One day, Squirrel said to Tortoise, "My friend, we have no money, but market day is getting close.

What business can we do to make some money?"

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0054_bi-imu-ijapa-se-ri-konbo.md p1; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Marleen Visser

claims.locator: raw/asp/yo/0054_bi-imu-ijapa-se-ri-konbo.md p1; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Marleen Visser

items.text: Ní ọjọ́ ọjà, Ìjàpá lọ sí ọjà. Ó rí àwọn méjì ní ọ̀ọ́kán tí wón ń jà. Kíá, ó gbé àwọn abọ́ rẹ̀ sílẹ̀, ó sì lọ síbi ìjà náà.

translation_en.text:
On the day of the market,

Tortoise went to the marketplace.

He saw two people fighting in the distance. He put down his clay plates and went to watch the fight.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0054_bi-imu-ijapa-se-ri-konbo.md p3; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Marleen Visser

translation_en.text:
Immediately, without finding out what caused the fight,

Tortoise took a big stick and began to beat Mole. "Leave my friend alone!" shouted Tortoise.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0054_bi-imu-ijapa-se-ri-konbo.md p5; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Marleen Visser

items.text: Ní ọjọ́ ọjà kan, ọkùnrin kan yá ẹsẹ̀ láti ọwọ́ ọkùnrin kan, ó tún yá apá àti ara lọ́wọ́ ẹlòmíràn. Lẹ́hìn náà, ọkùnrin yìí pa gbogbo ẹ̀yà yìí pọ̀ pẹ̀lú orí rẹ̀. Ó sì lọ sí ọjà.

translation_en.text:
One market day, a man
borrowed legs from another
man, and arms from another,
and a body from a third man.
Then this man joined all the
parts together. He put his head
on top and went to the market.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0091_adùn-ọmọ-arẹwà-kan.md p2; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

items.label: beta

items.text: Ọkùnrin yìí fẹ́ Adùn, ó sì pinu láti fẹ́ ẹ. Adùn náà fẹ́ràn ìmúra ọkùnrin yìí, ó sì fẹ́ wà pẹ̀lú rẹ̀. Ọkùnrin yìí wá láti ìlú jínjìn. Adùn sì pinu láti padà pẹ̀lú rẹ̀.

translation_en.text:
This man wanted Adun and was
determined to marry her. Adun
was pleased by his appearance.
She wanted to be with him. The
man came from a far town, and
Adun decided to return with
him.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0091_adùn-ọmọ-arẹwà-kan.md p3; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

can_do: C2.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C2
items.text: Bí Adùn àti ọkùnrin náà ṣe ń lọ́ sí ìlú rẹ̀, ẹni tó ni ẹsẹ̀ gba ẹsẹ̀ náà padà. Lẹ́hìn náà, ẹni tó ni apá gba apá náà padà. Ẹni tó ni ara náà gba ara náà padà.

translation_en.text:
As Adun and the man journeyed
to his place, the owner of the
legs took the legs back.
Then the owner of the arms
took his arms back.
And finally the owner of the
body took that back.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0091_adùn-ọmọ-arẹwà-kan.md p4; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

items.text: Lẹ́hìn náà, Adùn lọ bá babaláwo láti mọ nǹkan tí òun lè ṣe. Babaláwo náà sọ fún, “Lọ ra àwọn àkàrà. Fi àwọn kan sínú epo pupa, kí o sì fi sínú ìho Ìjàpá.”

translation_en.text:
Eventually Adun consulted a
diviner about what to do. The
diviner advised, "Go and buy
some bean cakes. Soak them in
palm oil and put them in
Tortoise's horn."

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0091_adùn-ọmọ-arẹwà-kan.md p10; Text: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

can_do: C2.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C2
items.text: Ní ọjọ́ kejì, ó kó àwọn nǹkan rẹ̀, ó sì bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í sá lọ. Nígbà tí Ìjàpá mú ìho láti fọn, àwọn àkàrà aládùn náà bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í jábọ́ sí ẹnu rẹ̀.

translation_en.text:
The following day, she took her
things and began to run away
again. When Tortoise took the
horn to blow it, the delicious
bean cakes fell into his mouth.

items.text: Bí ó ṣe ń kàwé si ni ó ń ri bí òun ṣe fẹ́ràn àwọn ènìyàn Kenya. Ó fẹ́ jẹ́ kí wọ́n ní ayọ̀ àtí òmìnira. Bí ó ṣe ń kàwé si ni ó ń rántí ilé rẹ̀ ní Afrika.

translation_en.text:
The more she learnt, the more she realised that she loved the people of Kenya. She wanted them to be happy and free.

The more she learnt, the more she remembered her African home.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0110_eso-kekere-kan-itan-ti-wangari-maathai.md p7; Text: Nicola Rijsdijk; Illustration: Maya Marshak

items.text: Nígbá tí ó parí ẹ̀kọ́ rẹ̀, ó padà sí Kenya. Ṣùgbọ́n orílẹ̀-èdè rẹ̀ ti yípadà. Àwọn oko ńlá ti pọ̀si nílẹ̀. Àwọn obìnrin kò ní igi láti fi dáná. Àwọn ènìyàn tòṣì. Ebi sì ń pa àwọn ọmọdé.

translation_en.text: When she had finished her studies, she returned to Kenya. But her country had changed. Huge farms stretched across the land. Women had no wood to make cooking fires. The people were poor and the children were hungry.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0110_eso-kekere-kan-itan-ti-wangari-maathai.md p8; Text: Nicola Rijsdijk; Illustration: Maya Marshak

items.text: Lẹ́hìn àkókò púpọ̀, àwọn igi tuntun náà dàgbà sí igbó, àwọn odò náà sì padà. Gbogbo ènìyàn ní Afrika ni ó gbọ́ nǹkan tí Wangari ṣe. Lónìí, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn igi ni ó ti dàgbà nípasẹ èso ti Wangari.

translation_en.text: As time passed, the new trees grew into forests, and the rivers started flowing again. Wangari's message spread across Africa. Today, millions of trees have grown from Wangari's seeds.

sources.locator: raw/asp/yo/0110_eso-kekere-kan-itan-ti-wangari-maathai.md p10; Text: Nicola Rijsdijk; Illustration: Maya Marshak

items.label: beta

can_do: C2.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C2
items.text: Wangari tí ṣiṣẹ́ gan an. Gbogbo ènìyàn káàkiri àgbáyé ni ó mọ̀, wọ́n sì fun ní ẹ̀bùn ńlá kan. Wọ́n ń pè é ní ẹ̀bùn ti Nobel Peace, òun sì ni obìnrin àkọ́kọ́ tí ó kọ́kọ́ gbà á.

translation_en.text: Wangari had worked hard. People all over the world took notice, and gave her a famous prize. It is called the Nobel Peace Prize, and she was the first African woman ever to receive it.

items.text: Ọba náà wí fún Eerin àti Ọ̀gà pé “ mo fẹ́ kí ẹ máa fi ẹsẹ̀ janlẹ̀ títí omi yòó fi rú jádé.” Ọba ṣe ìlèrí láti fi ọmọbìnrin rẹ̀ fún ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá lè ṣe àṣeyọrí.

translation_en.text:
The kind said to Elephant and
Chameleon, "I want you to
stomp
on the ground with your feet
until water comes out."
The king promised the princess
in marriage to the one who
succeeded.

translation_en.text:
Chameleon had no hope since
he was very small.
Elephant was extremely happy
since he was so big and
powerful.
Elephant went to the field and
started stomping on the
ground.

items.text: Eruku bo ilẹ̀, ṣùgbọ́n omi kò jáde. Eerin fi ẹsẹ̀ janlẹ̀ títí omi fi fẹ́ bẹ́rẹ́ sí i sun jáde, ṣùgbọ́n ó ti rẹ̀ ẹ́. Ó fún Ọ̀gà ní àyè láti gbìyànjú.

translation_en.text:
A lot of dust came, but no
water.
Elephant stomped on the
ground until water was almost
coming out, but he was too
tired.
He gave Chameleon a chance
to try.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the sky,

Sun was ready to leave her sister.

She kissed the moon goodbye and went home.
